newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serb cooperation pact criticised.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb cooperation pact criticised.

text.p: Moslem leaders said on Monday that a pact between Bosnian Serbs and neighbouring Yugoslavia violated the peace agreement and showed the Belgrade government still harboured territorial ambitions in Bosnia.

Yugoslavia and Bosnia's Serb entity signed a comprehensive cooperation accord last week covering economic and defence policy without seeking the approval of the new peacetime central government in Bosnia.

The Moslem chairman of the Bosnian collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and the Moslem co-prime minister, Haris Silajdzic, issued a statement saying the pact violated the country's constitution under the Dayton peace accords.
The two leaders said a clause which called for mutual defence meant "a disruption in the balance of relations fixed by the Dayton agreement and could jeopardise peace in the whole region".
"The agreement shows that the regime in Belgrade has not given up its pretensions in Bosnia-Herzegovina although it is obliged to do so as a responsible party to the Dayton accords," they said.

Bosnian Serb authorities had no legal right to make unilateral agreements on foreign trade, border traffic, citizenship, customs and other issues which are specifically in the jurisdiction of the Bosnian central government, Izetbegovic and Silajdzic said.
Under the Dayton treaty, Bosnia has a central parliament, cabinet and presidency with members from each national community represented.
Leaders from the Serb entity or a Moslem-Croat entity can veto any measure which is considered a threat to vital interests.
A spokesman for the office of the international High Representative to Bosnia said the cooperation pact carried no legal weight without the approval of the joint parliament.
"This draft agreement should not have been written without prior consultation with Republika Srpska's (the Serb republic) federation partners," Colum Murphy said.
Saying the pact violated the spirit of the Dayton treaty, Murphy said the cooperation pact marked a return of wartime Bosnian Serb nationalist rhetoric but he said it was "hopefully temporary".
